nodes.summary: Under `vs.Nodup`, an enumerated association list is recovered from its lookup function: there is no duplicate key for `getVal` to shadow, so the list is exactly the association list built from its own lookups.
nodes.title: Enumerated lists over distinct variables are recovered from lookups

nodes.summary: Under `vs.Nodup`, distinct enumerated association lists denote distinct assignments: if two enumerated lists agree as lookup functions on `vs`, they are the same list. Without `Nodup` this fails, since a duplicate key lets a later entry be shadowed by an earlier one.
nodes.title: Enumerated lists over distinct variables give distinct assignments

nodes.summary: Counting the assignment enumeration: the total (worst-case) size of the candidate search space is `(wordsUpToCount B) ^ |vs|`. This counts enumerated association lists; see the cost model in the module header for when it coincides with the number of distinct assignments.
nodes.title: Size of the bounded assignment enumeration

nodes.summary: All assignments of the variables in `vs` to words of length at most `B`, as association lists, each occurring once (as in `wordsUpTo`).
nodes.title: Enumeration of bounded assignments as association lists

nodes.summary: Soundness and completeness of the bounded-search specification: it reports `true` exactly when `φ` has a solution whose values on `vs` have length at most `B`. The hypothesis is that `vs` covers the variables of `φ`.
nodes.title: Soundness and completeness of the bounded-search specification

nodes.summary: The bounded-search specification: enumerate bounded assignments and check `φ` on each one. This is a classical specification, not an executable decision procedure: `assignLists` is `noncomputable`, so this Boolean cannot be evaluated by `decide`.
nodes.title: Bounded-search satisfiability specification

nodes.summary: A lookup returns one of the values in the list, so it inherits the length bound on values.
nodes.title: Lookup inherits the length bound on values

nodes.summary: Lookup in the association list built from an assignment returns the assignment.
nodes.title: Lookup recovers the assignment from its association list

nodes.summary: Lookup in an association list; unbound variables read as `[]`.
nodes.title: Association-list lookup defaulting to the empty word

nodes.summary: The keys of the association list built from an assignment are the variables themselves.
nodes.title: Keys of the association list built from an assignment

nodes.summary: Membership in the assignment enumeration: the keys are exactly `vs` and every value has length at most `B`.
nodes.title: Membership in the bounded assignment enumeration

nodes.summary: Membership in the exact-length enumeration is exactly the length equality.
nodes.title: Membership in the exact-length word enumeration

nodes.summary: Membership in the enumeration is exactly the length bound.
nodes.title: Membership in the bounded-length word enumeration

nodes.summary: The empty word is enumerated at every bound.
nodes.title: Empty word is in every bounded enumeration

nodes.summary: Summing a constant over a list.
nodes.title: Sum of a constant over a list

nodes.summary: Counting the exact-length enumeration: `|Σ| ^ n` words.
nodes.title: Size of the exact-length word enumeration

nodes.summary: All words of length exactly `n` over a finite alphabet, each occurring once: each step extends only the words of the previous length, never the whole `wordsUpTo` enumeration, so no word is duplicated.
nodes.title: Words of a given length over a finite alphabet

nodes.summary: The number of words of length at most `B`: `∑_{n ≤ B} |Σ| ^ n`.
nodes.title: Number of words of length at most $B$

nodes.summary: Counting the enumeration: `∑_{n ≤ B} |Σ| ^ n` words, the number of distinct words of length at most `B`.
nodes.title: Size of the bounded-length word enumeration

nodes.summary: All words of length at most `B` over a finite alphabet, each occurring once: the concatenation of the exact-length layers `0, …, B`.
nodes.title: Words of length at most $B$ over a finite alphabet

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
